seo.title: TablePro vs Beekeeper Studio: free and paid features
seo.description: Beekeeper Studio is an open-source Electron client for Windows, macOS and Linux. TablePro is open source and native. Compare tiers, engines, AI and import.

header.title: TablePro vs Beekeeper Studio
header.lead: Beekeeper Studio and TablePro are open-source database clients with different free and paid features. Beekeeper Studio uses {technology}; TablePro uses native drivers.

tablepro: Oracle, Cassandra and Snowflake without a paid tier.
Free AI chat and MCP, with your choice of AI provider.
A native app with a separate free iPhone and iPad app.
competitor: The same client on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Firebird, SQL Anywhere or GreengageDB connections.
Cloud workspaces for sharing connections and queries, from {cells.sync.edition}.

glance.intro: Both clients are open source and both have a Vim mode in the SQL editor. Each has an ER diagram: free in TablePro, and in every paid tier of Beekeeper Studio.

diagram.label: ER diagram
diagram.tablepro: A read-only ER diagram, exported as PNG or SQL, free

vim.label: Vim mode
vim.tablepro: Free, in the SQL editor, with motions, registers and macros

importExport.label: Import, export and backup
importExport.tablepro: Free in the Mac app: import CSV, JSON, XLSX and SQL files, export to CSV, JSON, SQL, XLSX and other formats, and Backup Dump and Restore Dump where the engine has a dump tool

lifetimeLicense.label: After a subscription ends
lifetimeLicense.tablepro: A monthly or yearly plan’s paid features lock when it ends. A one-time purchase has no expiry date

items.text: It connects to engines TablePro does not support, such as Firebird, SQL Anywhere and GreengageDB.
From the {cells.sync.edition} tier, cloud workspaces sync and share connections and queries with colleagues on any of its platforms.
TablePro is a Mac app written in Swift, with native database drivers. Beekeeper Studio is built on {technology}. Both offer separate builds for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
TablePro includes every supported engine for free. Beekeeper Studio Community includes PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and SQLite; Oracle, Cassandra and Snowflake require paid tiers.
The <link>AI assistant and the MCP server</link> are free in the Mac app, with the AI provider you choose. Beekeeper Studio’s AI Shell needs a paid tier.

<link>Importing and exporting data</link> is free in TablePro, and so are backups through an engine’s own dump tool where it has one. Beekeeper Studio lists Import/Export & Backup/Restore in its paid tiers, not in Community.
TablePro is open source under the AGPLv3, including the code of its paid features. Beekeeper Studio’s Community edition is open source under {licence}.
<link>iCloud Sync</link> syncs connections across Macs, iPhones and iPads. It requires Starter on the Mac and is free on iPhone and iPad.
The separate <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> is free, with no in-app purchases. Beekeeper Studio has no mobile app.
TablePro requires a supported driver. Check the <link>supported databases</link> before you switch.
The ER diagram is free but read-only: you change tables in the Structure tab, not by drawing them.

Beekeeper Studio’s license covers versions released while you paid; monthly plans qualify after 12 months. TablePro subscriptions lock paid features when they end, while the free app remains available. A one-time TablePro purchase has no expiry date.

switching.intro: Import Beekeeper Studio’s local workspace connections. The app can stay closed, and its files are not changed.
steps: In TablePro, choose <ui>File > Import > Import from Other App…</ui>

Select Beekeeper Studio and turn on <ui>Include passwords</ui>. TablePro decrypts the passwords Beekeeper Studio saved, including SSH passwords and key passphrases, so there is nothing to approve in the Keychain.

Review the list, decide what happens to any duplicates, and click <ui>Import</ui>. Folders become groups, connection colors and SSL settings come across, and an SSH bastion host becomes a jump host. A connection to an engine TablePro does not support arrives unchecked.
Before you remove Beekeeper Studio, open a connection that had a password to check that it came across.
after: Connections in a Beekeeper Studio cloud workspace are not imported, only those in the local workspace.
Saved queries, query history and keyboard shortcuts stay in Beekeeper Studio.

faq.question: Does TablePro run natively on Apple silicon?
faq.answer: Yes. TablePro has separate builds for Apple silicon and for Intel Macs, and <link>the download page</link> offers both.

faq.question: I use Vim mode in Beekeeper Studio. Does TablePro have one?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is free. Turn on <ui>Settings > Editor > Vim mode</ui> for motions, registers and macros, where :w runs the query.

notes.beekeeper-databases: Community covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server and others. Paid tiers add more, such as Oracle, Cassandra and Snowflake.
notes.beekeeper-ai-shell: AI Shell, in paid tiers only, not in Community
notes.beekeeper-cloud-workspaces: Cloud workspaces that sync and share connections and queries, from the {edition} tier
notes.beekeeper-erd-paid: In every paid tier, not in Community
notes.beekeeper-import-export-paid: Import/Export & Backup/Restore, in every paid tier, not in Community
notes.beekeeper-lifetime-license: A yearly plan, or 12 months in a row on a monthly plan, lets you keep using the paid features of the versions released while you paid, after the subscription ends. Cloud workspaces need an active subscription.
